metadata.hardware_requirements: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a com-puting server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores).

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Preprocessed video data, where vehicle locations are extracted from traffic video frames and reformed as position matrices, used as inputs for the DRL method.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Access 'upon request' from the corresponding author, no public link or DOI provided.

nodes_source.source_quote: The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_source.description: Data used to calibrate the simulation parameters for driving behaviors.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Mentioned as used for calibration, but no specific source or access path is provided.

nodes_process.node_name: Extract vehicle locations from video frames
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations (x, y) are extracted from raw traffic video frames.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, no params stated

nodes_process.node_name: Create position matrix from vehicle locations
nodes_process.source_quote: traffic state at time step t is represented by a position matrix m_t in R^XxY; m_t(x, y) = U_v, i in I_t, where U_v is a constant and I_t refers to the set of vehicles in the control area at time step t.
nodes_process.description: Traffic state at time t is represented as a position matrix m_t. Vehicle locations are marked with a constant U_v, and signal states (U_G, U_R) are included. Other elements are set to zero.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, 0/3 params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: For computation efficiency, down-sampling is introduced before the matrix stack to reduce the input dimensions and maintain sufficient information about vehicle positions.
nodes_process.description: Down-sample the position matrix to reduce input dimensions and maintain sufficient information about vehicle positions for computational efficiency.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, no tools mentioned, no params stated

nodes_process.node_name: Stack matrices for DRL state representation
nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s_t: S_t = {m_t-(N-1),..., m_t}.
nodes_process.description: Matrices of consecutive N time steps are stacked to represent the state s_t, capturing vehicle dynamics for the DRL method.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, 1/1 params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r_t after action a_t is defined by the following: r_t = mu*v_t + omega*q_t, mu > 0, omega < 0
nodes_process.description: The reward function r_t is defined based on the average speed (v_t) in the merging area and the average queue length (q_t) at the on-ramp, with positive weight mu for speed and negative weight omega for queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, 2/2 params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: the Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: The Q-network architecture, a deep neural network, is defined based on a revision of Mnih et al. [30]'s network. It comprises three CNN layers and one FC layer for each output layer, as detailed in Figure 7.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all tools implicitly named, all params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The gradient-based algorithm Adam [28] is used to update w_i to minimize the loss function. ... The experience replay [30] stores the data ... The target network [29] is introduced...
nodes_process.description: The Deep Q-network is trained using the Adam optimizer to minimize a loss function. The training incorporates experience replay and a target network for stability, and a multitask learning strategy to predict speed and queue length simultaneously.
tools_mentioned: Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 3/5 tools named, all params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies...
nodes_process.description: The PI-ALINEA method is set up as a baseline. It fixes the green phase length and determines the red phase length based on previous cycle's red phase and downstream occupancies, using regulator parameters KR and Kp.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, 3/3 params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31]. The simulation is performed in the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China...
nodes_process.description: A microscopic traffic simulation environment is set up using SUMO, modeling a freeway section in Qingdao and Huangdao, China. It includes an on-ramp, mainline, and merging area, with driving behavior parameters calibrated using empirical data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 tools named, all params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: 20 simulation experiments are conducted for each scenario (no-control, PI-ALINEA, DRL) within the SUMO environment. Simulations for both training and evaluation phases are initialized with different random seeds.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 tools named, 1/2 params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_process.description: The Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) percentiles of travel times in the mainline are evaluated and presented for the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, no params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: Mean vehicle travel times from 20 simulation experiments are presented for the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, no params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_process.description: The temporal-spatial distribution of mean speeds along the mainline is analyzed and visualized for the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, no params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_process.description: The Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) percentiles of queue lengths at the on-ramp are evaluated and presented for the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, no params stated

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate queue lengths and red ratios
nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time) in each simulation for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_process.description: The relationship between mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and red ratios (proportion of red phase) is analyzed for PI-ALINEA and DRL methods.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, no params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_process.description: The relationship between queue lengths at the on-ramp and occupancy downstream of the merging area is analyzed for PI-ALINEA and DRL methods.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, no params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_process.description: Traffic flows downstream of the merge area are evaluated and compared for the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, no params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: As shown in Figure 15, the control area is divided into eight subareas.
nodes_process.description: The control area is divided into eight distinct subareas for the purpose of conducting a perturbation analysis.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, 1/1 params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The information in the subarea is removed from original data to generate perturbed data for each subarea.
nodes_process.description: Perturbed data is generated for each subarea by systematically removing the information corresponding to that subarea from the original simulation data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, no params stated

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate travel time with perturbed data
nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_process.description: Travel times are evaluated using perturbed input data, where information from different subareas is removed. Results are compared against a baseline using original data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools mentioned, no params stated
